faqs.q: Sec. 54-175. - Parking and displaying vehicles for sale upon private property.
faqs.a:
(a)
The city council finds and declares that the parking of vehicles upon private property
               of another for the principal purpose of displaying such vehicle for sale is detrimental
               to the public health, safety, and general welfare of the citizens of the municipality,
               and that regulation of such activity on private property is a permissible regulation
               of the aesthetics of the community.
(b)
No person shall park a vehicle upon private property belonging to another for the
               principal purpose of displaying such vehicle for sale.
(c)
It shall be unlawful for the owner of any property located within the city to allow
               vehicles owned by others to be parked on such property for the principal purpose of
               being offered for sale.
(d)
Whenever a parked vehicle displays a sign or message indicating that it is being offered
               for sale, such display shall be prima facie evidence that the vehicle is parked for
               the principal purpose of being displayed for sale.
(e)
For purposes of this section only, the term "vehicle" shall include any device capable
               of being moved from place to place upon wheels or tracks, as well as devices capable
               of being moved on or through water or air, such as boats and airplanes.
(f)
The provisions of this section shall not apply upon land zoned by the city to permit
               commercial sales of vehicles.
(
Ord. No. 4561, § 2, 8-29-2016
)
